raw.details:
Overview

Event Details

  • Event Name: Symbiosis Skill Hackathon (SSH-2027)
  • Organized By: Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences (SUAS), Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India
  • Mode: Offline (On-Campus)
  • Event Dates: 22–23 February 2027
  • Duration: 36 Hours
  • Team Size: 1–4 Members
  • Registration Deadline: To be confirmed before publishing
  • Eligibility: Undergraduate and Postgraduate Students, including Engineering Students and Inter College Students

About Symbiosis Skill Hackathon (SSH-2027)

Innovate. Build. Compete. Make an Impact!

Get ready for Symbiosis Skill Hackathon 2.0 (SSH-2027), a national-level, 36-hour hackathon organized by Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences (SUAS), Indore, on 22–23 February 2027. Bringing together talented innovators, developers, and aspiring entrepreneurs from across India, SSH-2027 challenges participants to transform bold ideas into impactful, technology-driven solutions for real-world problems.

Explore cutting-edge domains, including Generative AI and Agentic AI, Cybersecurity and AI Security, Cloud-Native Development and DevSecOps, IoT and Robotics, Physical AI, Blockchain and Web3, Data Science, EdTech, AR/VR and Extended Reality (XR), and Quantum Computing. Collaborate with like-minded innovators, learn from expert mentors, develop working prototypes, and showcase your solutions before a panel of judges.

Push boundaries, embrace emerging technologies, and turn your ideas into innovations that matter. Your journey from idea to impact starts at SSH-2027!

Eligibility Guidelines

  • Eligible Participants: The hackathon is open to students currently studying in Class 12, undergraduate, or postgraduate programmes at recognized schools and institutions across India.
  • Academic Disciplines: Students from all academic streams and disciplines are welcome to participate, subject to the event's registration requirements.
  • Team Composition: Teams must comply with the prescribed team size and registration guidelines. Inter-school, inter-college, and interdisciplinary teams are permitted subject to the rules announced by the organizing committee.
  • Student Verification: Participants must provide a valid school/college ID card or proof of current enrollment when requested by the organizing committee.
  • Registration Accuracy: All registration details must be accurate and verifiable. Providing false information or misrepresenting eligibility may result in disqualification.
  • Rules and Conduct: All participants must maintain academic integrity and comply with the official hackathon rules, submission requirements, and code of conduct.
  • Final Eligibility Decision: The organizing committee reserves the right to verify eligibility and make decisions regarding participation in accordance with the published event guidelines.

Team Formation and Guidelines

  • Team Size: Each team must consist of 1–4 members, including individual participants.
  • Single-Team Registration: Each participant may register with only one team and cannot participate in multiple teams.
  • Team Formation: Teams may be formed before the event or finalized during the Ideation and Networking Mixer, subject to approval by the organizing committee.
  • Mixed and Inter-Institutional Teams: Teams may include students from Class 12, undergraduate, and postgraduate programmes, including participants from different schools, colleges, institutions, and academic disciplines, provided all members meet the eligibility criteria.
  • Team Formation Assistance: The organizing committee may assist individual participants in finding teammates, subject to availability.
  • Problem Statement Selection: Each team may select and work on only one problem statement throughout the hackathon.
  • Team Composition Changes: Team composition must remain unchanged once the hackathon begins. Any exceptional change requires prior approval from the organizing committee.
  • Registration and Eligibility: All team members must provide accurate registration details and satisfy the eligibility requirements. Duplicate participation or misrepresentation may result in disqualification.
  • Collective Responsibility: Each team is collectively responsible for its submission, originality, compliance with the hackathon rules, and timely completion of all required deliverables.

Hackathon Domains

Participants will develop solutions in one of the following technology domains:

  • Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI & Agentic AI
  • Cybersecurity, AI Security & Digital Trust
  • Web Development, Cloud-Native Applications & DevSecOps
  • Mobile Application Development & AI-Powered Applications
  • Internet of Things (IoT), Robotics & Physical AI
  • Blockchain, Web3 & Decentralized Applications
  • EdTech, AI-Powered Learning & Educational Innovation
  • Data Science, Big Data & Intelligent Analytics
  • AR/VR, Extended Reality (XR) & Immersive Technologies
  • Quantum Computing & Post-Quantum Cryptography

The problem statements will be announced during the offline round and will focus on industry requirements and societal challenges. Teams will finalize their problem statements during the Final Briefing Session.

Stages and Timelines

Stage 1: Online Registration and PPT Submission (Submission through Unstop)

Eligible teams must complete online registration and submit a project proposal for preliminary evaluation during Stage 1. Teams may choose a problem statement from Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2026 or propose their own innovative solution to a real-world problem.

Stage 2 (Offline Round): Shortlisted teams must work on a problem statement from the list provided by the organizers, as per the event guidelines.

Hackathon Project Proposal

  • Problem Statement: Define the problem and its significance.
  • Proposed Solution: Describe the solution and its key features.
  • Target Users/Use Case: Identify the intended users and practical applications.
  • Technology and AI/ML Approach: Explain the technologies, tools, and AI/ML techniques (if applicable) proposed for developing the solution.
  • Proposed TinyFish Integration: Explain how TinyFish can support web interaction, data extraction, or workflow automation, wherever applicable.
  • Expected Impact: Highlight anticipated benefits and expected outcomes.
  • Feasibility and Implementation Plan: Briefly explain the technical feasibility of the proposed solution, required resources, technologies, and planned implementation approach.

Submission Requirements

  • PowerPoint Presentation: Teams must prepare a presentation containing 5–9 slides using the official PPT template provided by the organizing committee. The presentation should cover the problem statement, proposed solution, innovation, technology stack, implementation approach, and expected impact.
  • GitHub Repository: Teams must provide a GitHub repository link containing the project code, prototype, or relevant initial implementation. A fully developed working prototype is not mandatory at this stage. The repository must be accessible to the evaluation panel.
  • Project Originality: The proposed solution must be original. Any pre-existing code, third-party resources, open-source components, or AI-assisted contributions must be appropriately acknowledged wherever applicable.
  • Submission Process: Teams must submit their completed PPT and GitHub repository link through the designated registration or submission platform before the prescribed deadline.

Evaluation and Shortlisting

  • Submissions will be evaluated based on problem relevance, innovation, technical feasibility, implementation approach, potential impact, and clarity of presentation.
  • The organizing committee will shortlist teams based on the preliminary evaluation and available offline participation capacity.
  • Shortlisted teams will be invited to participate in the offline hackathon at Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences (SUAS), Indore.
  • Shortlisting results and further instructions will be communicated through the official event channels.

Important Instructions

  • Each team may submit only one project proposal for one problem statement.
  • All submitted information must be accurate, and teams must comply with the official eligibility criteria and code of conduct.
  • The organizing committee must confirm the PPT submission deadline, registration closing date, submission platform, and shortlisting announcement date before publication.
  • The organizing committee reserves the right to reject incomplete, inaccessible, late, or non-compliant submissions.
  • Present all nine sections in the project proposal PPT.
  • Use clear explanations, diagrams, or workflow illustrations wherever appropriate.
  • Demonstrate the practical relevance and feasibility of the proposed solution.
  • Clearly explain the role of AI/ML and TinyFish, where applicable.
  • Focus on innovation, technical implementation, real-world impact, and future scalability.
  • Teams will be evaluated based on their PPT submissions and profiles.

Stage 2: Offline Building Round + Mentorship Round (22 Feb 27, 09:00 AM)

  • Dates: 22–23 February 2027
  • Venue: Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences, Indore, Madhya Pradesh
  • Mode: On-campus
  • Duration: 36 Hours

Grand Finale Round

Teams will continue building and refining their projects before the final evaluation. The hackathon will conclude with the Grand Finale, where teams will present their completed solution before the judging panel. Teams will also participate in a Q&A session with the judges.

The offline round will include registration and check-in, inauguration, problem statement briefing, team coding, mentor interactions, project evaluation, and the closing ceremony.

Hackathon Format and Process

The event will follow the stages outlined below:

  • Participant Registration and Team Check-in
  • Inauguration Ceremony and Rule Briefing
  • Keynote Address
  • Ideation and Networking Mixer
  • Problem Statement Announcement and Finalization
  • Continuous Coding and Prototype Development
  • Mentor Interaction and Review Rounds
  • Final Submission and Code Freeze
  • Project Expo and Final Judging
  • Closing Ceremony and Prize Distribution

The detailed schedule will be communicated to shortlisted participants by the organizing team.

Registration Fees and Mentorship

  • Registration Fee: ₹100 (non-refundable).
  • Offline Team Participation Fee: ₹1,500 for shortlisted teams invited to participate in the offline round (non-refundable).
  • Optional Mentorship: ₹399 for teams opting for additional mentorship support.

Please ensure that the applicable fee, payment process, and terms are communicated clearly during registration.

Rules and Code of Conduct

  • Compliance with Event Guidelines: All participants must follow the official event schedule, instructions, and guidelines issued by the organizing committee.
  • Team Composition and Registration: Teams must comply with the prescribed team size and registration requirements. Any changes to team members after registration require prior approval from the organizing committee.
  • Attendance and Participation: All registered team members must participate actively throughout the hackathon and comply with attendance, check-in, and reporting requirements.
  • Submission Deadlines and Code Freeze: All teams must adhere to the prescribed submission deadlines, code-freeze requirements, and other milestones announced by the organizing committee. Late submissions may not be accepted.
  • Development During the Hackathon: The submitted solution must be developed during the hackathon in accordance with the rules announced by the organizers. Pre-existing code, templates, and components may be used only to the extent permitted by the event rules and must be appropriately disclosed where required.
  • Use of Open-Source Tools and AI: Participants may use open-source tools, APIs, libraries, frameworks, generative AI tools, and AI coding assistants, subject to applicable licences and event rules. Teams are responsible for verifying the accuracy, security, functionality, and originality of AI-generated code and content.
  • Originality and Plagiarism: Teams must ensure that their submissions represent genuine work and must acknowledge third-party resources, datasets, libraries, code, and AI-generated contributions wherever required. Plagiarism, unauthorized reuse, misrepresentation, and submission of another team's work are prohibited.
  • Intellectual Property Rights: Teams must respect all applicable intellectual property rights and ensure that their solutions do not infringe third-party rights. Ownership, licensing, publication, and permitted use of submitted projects shall be governed by the intellectual property policy communicated by the organizing committee.
  • Submission Requirements: Teams must submit all required deliverables, including source code, project documentation, presentation slides, demonstration links, and other specified materials, through the prescribed platform before the deadline.
  • Project Demonstration and Evaluation: Teams must present and demonstrate their solutions to the jury at the allotted time. Evaluation will be based on the announced judging criteria. Failure to demonstrate the project without an approved reason may affect the team's evaluation.
  • Fair Competition: Teams must not engage in collusion, impersonation, unauthorized collaboration, manipulation of registrations or submissions, interference with other teams, or any attempt to influence the judging process improperly.
  • Cybersecurity and Data Privacy: Participants must not access, attack, disrupt, or modify systems, networks, accounts, or data without explicit authorization. Teams must handle personal, confidential, and sensitive data responsibly and comply with applicable data protection requirements.
  • Respectful Behaviour: All participants must treat fellow participants, mentors, judges, volunteers, and organizing staff with respect. Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, threats, abusive behaviour, and other forms of misconduct will not be tolerated.
  • Venue Facilities and Safety: Participants must comply with venue rules, safety guidelines, and security instructions. Any damage to institutional property, misuse of equipment, or violation of safety procedures may result in disciplinary action.
  • Overnight Coding and Accommodation: Participants using designated overnight coding zones or accommodation facilities must follow the prescribed access timings, security procedures, and venue instructions. Only authorized participants may access restricted areas.
  • Disqualification and Disciplinary Action: Violation of event rules, plagiarism, misconduct, unauthorized access, or other serious breaches may result in warnings, penalties, removal from the venue, or disqualification, as determined by the organizing committee.
  • Appeals and Grievances: Any grievance or appeal concerning event procedures, eligibility, or disciplinary action must be submitted to the organizing committee through the prescribed process and within the specified timeframe.
  • Amendments to Rules: The organizing committee reserves the right to clarify, modify, or introduce rules when necessary. Any changes will be communicated through official event channels.
  • Final Authority: The decisions of the jury regarding technical evaluation, scoring, and rankings shall be final and binding. The organizing committee shall have final authority over event administration, eligibility, and the interpretation and enforcement of these rules.

Mentorship and Evaluation Criteria

Participants will receive opportunities to interact with industry experts, startup founders, and SUAS faculty members.

Projects will be evaluated on the following criteria:

  • Innovation and Originality
  • Relevance to the Problem Statement
  • Technical Feasibility
  • Quality of Implementation
  • Practical Applicability and Potential Impact
  • Presentation and Clarity

Awards and Recognition

  • Total Prize Pool: Up to ₹3,00,000 in cash prizes, subject to final approval and the official prize distribution announced by the organizing committee.
  • Winner and Runner-Up Awards: Cash prizes and recognition will be awarded to the top-performing teams based on jury evaluation and the announced judging criteria.
  • Consolation Prizes: Consolation prizes may be awarded to selected teams demonstrating exceptional creativity, innovation, technical excellence, or promising solutions, as determined by the jury.
  • Certificates of Participation: Certificates will be provided to eligible participants who fulfil the event's participation requirements.
  • Special Recognition: Outstanding projects demonstrating innovation, feasibility, scalability, and real-world impact may receive special recognition.
  • Incubation and Mentorship Opportunities: Selected teams may receive post-event incubation, mentorship, or further development opportunities, subject to institutional policies, eligibility, and availability.
  • Prize Distribution: Prize categories, amounts, consolation prizes, and distribution procedures will be announced officially by the organizing committee and will be subject to applicable institutional policies and legal requirements.

Facilities and On-Campus Support

The following facilities will be provided to eligible participants during the offline event of Symbiosis Skill Hackathon 2.0 (SSH-2027), subject to availability and the conditions outlined below.

  • 22 February 2027 – Lunch and Dinner: Lunch and dinner will be provided to all teams registered for the offline event.
  • 23 February 2027 – Breakfast and Lunch: Breakfast and lunch will be provided to shortlisted teams participating in the offline round.
  • Overnight Accommodation: Basic on-campus accommodation in designated rest areas will be provided for outstation participants for the night of 22 February 2027 only, subject to availability, capacity, and applicable accommodation guidelines. Accommodation for any other night will not be provided unless explicitly announced by the organizing committee.
  • Overnight Coding Zones: Designated coding spaces will be available for participants during the hackathon, subject to venue rules and access guidelines.
  • Medical Assistance: Medical assistance will be available during the event for participants requiring support.
  • Security Support: On-campus security arrangements will be maintained during the event. Participants must follow all security instructions and access restrictions.
  • Food Stalls: Food stalls will be available on campus on a pay-per-order basis. Any purchases beyond the meals explicitly provided by the organizers will be at the participants' own expense.
  • Electrical Extension Boards: Participants must bring their own electrical extension boards or power strips suitable for their laptops and other essential devices. The organizers will not provide individual extension boards, multi-plug adapters, or personal charging accessories. Participants must use electrical equipment safely and comply with the instructions issued by the organizing committee.
  • Personal Devices and Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, development equipment, and other essential accessories. Specialized hardware, software, paid subscriptions, cloud services, and other project-specific resources will not be provided unless explicitly announced.
  • Internet and Power Supply: Internet connectivity and electricity will be available in designated areas, subject to infrastructure capacity and technical limitations. Uninterrupted internet access and power supply are not guaranteed.
  • Travel and Personal Expenses: Participants are responsible for their own travel, local transportation, and personal expenses unless otherwise specified by the organizing committee.
  • Off-Campus Accommodation: Participants requiring accommodation beyond the on-campus facility may refer to the list of suggested hotels and accommodation options shared by the organizing committee. Such accommodation will be arranged and paid for directly by the participants on an actual usage basis. All booking charges, transportation, and other related expenses will be borne by the participants. The organizing committee will not be responsible for hotel bookings or accommodation charges.
  • Safety and Personal Belongings: Participants are responsible for the security of their personal belongings and must use campus facilities responsibly. Any damage to institutional property or misuse of electrical equipment may result in disciplinary action.
  • Mandatory Identity Verification: All participants must carry one valid government-issued photo identity proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Driving Licence, or Passport) along with their valid School/Institution ID Card. Both identity documents are mandatory for entry, registration, and verification during the offline round. Participants failing to produce both documents may be denied entry to the event.

Participants are advised to review the accommodation guidelines and follow all instructions issued by the organizing committee. The availability of facilities is subject to venue capacity, safety requirements, and the official event guidelines.

 Join the Innovation Challenge!

Bring your ideas to life, collaborate with talented innovators, and build solutions that make a difference.

Register for the Symbiosis Skill Hackathon (SSH-2027) and take your innovation to the next level!

Organized by Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences (SUAS), Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India.
